testPolicy.text: Standardized testing is a required element of the application. Students who attend high school in the United States must submit the SAT or ACT (superscored). Students attending high school outside the US may instead use three AP exams, IB Diploma predicted or final results, British A-Level predicted or final results, or final results of an equivalent national exam (e.g. WASSCE, CAPE, French Baccalaureate, CBSE, ICSE, KCSE).

cost.totalIncludes: Three-term academic year: tuition 71,697 + fees 2,157 + housing 13,032 + food 8,496 + books/course materials 1,005 + personal 2,040. Not included: one-time 269 records and class dues fee and 250 orientation meals for first-time students; travel not in the budget (CDS G5 lists 608 transportation). Dartmouth runs on the D-Plan quarter system; one term costs tuition 23,899.

aidPromise.text: Universal need-blind admission (including all international citizens, since January 2022) with 100% of demonstrated need met; aid packages do not include student loans. Families with total annual income below $125,000 and typical assets have a $0 parent contribution; families between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets get scholarships and/or grants covering full tuition (free tuition up to $175,000).

facts.text: Early Decision is decisive: for fall 2025, 768 of 3,552 Early Decision applicants were admitted (21.6%), against 931 of the other 24,678 applicants (3.8%); ED filled 45% of the admitted class.
Dartmouth is need-blind for every applicant, including international citizens, and meets 100% of demonstrated need without loans.
Families earning under $125,000 with typical assets pay no parent contribution, and those up to $175,000 have full tuition covered.
International students make up a large share of applicants: 8,163 of 28,230 applied from abroad for fall 2025 and 154 enrolled; only 516 applicants and 27 enrollees were New Hampshire residents.
Students outside the US can meet the testing requirement with AP, IB, A-Level or national exam results, but US high school students must submit the SAT or ACT.
Dartmouth's year-round quarter system (D-Plan) bills by term: 2026-27 tuition is $23,899 per term, $71,697 for the standard three terms.

When it extended need-blind admission to all international citizens in January 2022, Dartmouth described itself as the sixth college or university in the United States with universal need-blind admissions paired with a commitment to meet 100 percent of demonstrated need.
Under the D-Plan both the cost of attendance and aid are adjusted to the terms a student enrolls in, including a proration for 2-term or 4-term enrollment in a year.
